transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. What brings you in to see me?
My work physical is what got me here. The doctor said my weight was too low, but honestly I just feel lighter on my feet for basketball and not as weighed down working in the garage.
Have you been trying to limit how much you eat, or do you feel anxious about gaining weight?

Most days, yeah, I keep it pretty simple—coffee in the morning, then maybe a small sandwich or half of whatever's around later. With the shop running late and the house busy, I feel better sticking to my own rules about it.
When you look in the mirror or think about your body, do you see yourself as too fat or worry that you might gain weight, even though your doctor says you're underweight?
Yeah. If the scale goes up even a pound, or my jeans start feeling tighter, I think I’m getting soft. I worry I’ll be slower moving around cars at work or up and down the court.
Can you tell me your current height and weight, and how much weight you've lost over the past few months?
I don’t have the exact numbers in my head. At the work physical they told me my weight was too low, but I honestly feel okay—lighter on my feet for basketball and less weighed down at the garage.
Could you tell me your exact current height and weight, even approximately, so I can calculate your BMI?
I don’t know the exact number. The work physical is what got me here—the doctor said my weight was too low. But I feel lighter on my feet playing basketball and less weighed down at the garage.
Have you noticed any physical changes like feeling unusually cold, dizzy, fatigued, or losing hair since you started cutting back on food?
I haven’t really noticed anything like that. I feel okay day to day.
Do you know roughly how much weight you’ve lost over the past few months, even if you don’t know your exact current weight?
I really don’t know how much. The work doctor just said I was too low. I’ve mostly noticed I feel lighter playing basketball and at work, not as weighed down.
Do you have any paperwork from your recent physical—like a printed height and weight—that I could use to calculate your BMI?
I don’t have any paperwork with me. The work doctor just told me my weight was too low. I mean, I feel lighter for basketball and less weighed down at the garage, so I didn’t think much of it.
Do you remember roughly what you used to weigh before all this, even a rough guess, so we can figure out about how many pounds or what percentage you've lost since then?

I don’t really have a number for what I used to weigh. The work physical is what got me here—they said I was too low. I just noticed I feel lighter playing basketball and less weighed down at the garage.
When people who know you well look at you now, do they say you look noticeably underweight or thin, or do you still look like you're within a normal weight range to them?
Nobody’s really said much to me about how I look. The work doctor said my weight was too low, but I just feel lighter on my feet playing basketball and less weighed down at the garage.
Have you had to buy noticeably smaller clothes or belt sizes recently because your old clothes are too loose, or do they still fit about the same as before?

I haven’t really paid attention to my clothes or belt size. The work doctor is the one who said my weight was too low. I just feel lighter for basketball and not as weighed down working at the garage.
Would you be willing to step on the scale here in the office right now so I can get an accurate current weight and height to calculate your BMI?
Yeah, I can step on it. The work physical doctor said my weight was too low, though I honestly just feel lighter on my feet for basketball and less weighed down at the garage.
Have you missed any menstrual periods, or has your cycle become irregular, since you started eating less?
I’m male, so I don’t have menstrual periods.
Now that you're on the scale, what does it show for your current weight, and can you also tell me your height?

I’m not sure what the number is. The work physical doctor just said my weight was too low. I mean, I feel lighter on the court and less weighed down at the garage, so it hasn’t felt like a problem to me.
I see you're on the scale now—can you look down and tell me exactly what number it shows for your weight?
I can see it, but I’m not really focused on the number. The work physical doctor said it was too low. I just feel lighter for basketball and not as weighed down working at the garage.
I really need the exact number showing on the scale right now—could you read it out loud to me?

I can see it, but I’m not going to read it out. The work physical doctor said it was too low—that’s what got me here. I just feel lighter on my feet for basketball and less weighed down at the garage.
It's okay if you don't want to say the number out loud—would it be alright if I just look at the scale myself right now to record your weight?
I'd rather not. The work physical doctor said it was too low, but I don't really see it as a problem—I just feel lighter for basketball and at the garage.
